### AD-1 — Layered modules with one-way dependencies

- **Binds:** all epics
- **Prevents:** rules written in routes or templates; one module reading or writing another module's tables
- **Rule:** web calls only its own module's service; services call other services, never another module's store; a store is imported only by its own service (and the seed CLI for `people.store`). Dependencies follow the diagram above and never point upward or in a cycle.

### AD-2 — Server-rendered HTML with htmx `[ASSUMPTION]`

- **Binds:** all epics, R16, RULE-9
- **Prevents:** one epic building a single-page app while another renders HTML; a second codebase and a JS build step
- **Rule:** every surface is a Jinja2 page served by FastAPI. Sheets, panels and refusals are htmx partial swaps (`hx-get`/`hx-post` returning HTML fragments). There is no JSON API and no JS framework or bundler in release one; htmx is a vendored static file. Every route also works on a full page load.

### AD-3 — One owner per table

- **Binds:** R1 to R16
- **Prevents:** two writers of bookings; epic-my-calendar writing its own booking queries
- **Rule:**

  | Tables | Sole writer | Others read through |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `offices`, `people` | seed CLI (AD-9) | `people.service` |
  | `rooms` | `rooms.service` | `rooms.service` |
  | `bookings`, `booking_attendees` | `bookings.service` | `bookings.service` |

  `calendar` owns no tables; it gets a person's bookings only from `bookings.service`.

### AD-4 — Overlaps and closed rooms refused by the database

- **Binds:** R5 (booking side), R7 to R11, RULE-1
- **Prevents:** double bookings when two people book at once; a code path (change, office-manager edit, settling a closed room's bookings) that forgets the check
- **Rule:** `BEFORE INSERT` and `BEFORE UPDATE` triggers on `bookings` raise `ABORT` when another row with the same `room_id` satisfies `other.start_at < NEW.end_at AND NEW.start_at < other.end_at` (half-open intervals, so back-to-back bookings are allowed), or when the room is closed. Every booking write runs in a transaction opened with `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`. `bookings.service` turns the abort into `BookingConflict` or `RoomClosed`. A service-level pre-check may run to build the refusal message and the "still free" suggestions, but the trigger is the guarantee.

### AD-5 — Times stored in UTC, shown in UK time

- **Binds:** R6 to R14, RULE-2
- **Prevents:** naive and aware datetimes mixed across epics; daylight-saving bugs; time-zone conversion done in more than one place
- **Rule:** `bookings.start_at` and `end_at` are UTC text `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:00Z`, so text order is time order. Conversion to and from `Europe/London` happens only in the web layer, through `roombooker/core/time.py` (zoneinfo). `bookings.service` checks 15-minute alignment and a length of 15 minutes to 4 hours; the table has `CHECK (end_at > start_at)`.

### AD-6 — One way to know the current person

- **Binds:** R1, R2, RULE-6
- **Prevents:** each epic reading identity in its own way
- **Rule:** the cookie `person_id` holds `people.id`, lasts 400 days, is `HttpOnly` and `SameSite=Lax`, and is not signed (RULE-6: anyone may pick anyone). The FastAPI dependency `core.current_person` is the only reader. It redirects to Pick your name when the cookie is missing or names an unknown or inactive person, then returns the person to the requested page.

### AD-7 — Authorisation lives in services

- **Binds:** R3 to R5, R9 to R11, R13, RULE-3, RULE-4
- **Prevents:** checks that exist only in the UI; epics defining "office manager" differently
- **Rule:** a service function that changes data takes the acting person and raises `NotAllowed` when RULE-3 or RULE-4 fails. Someone is an office manager of office X exactly when `people.is_office_manager` is true and `people.home_office_id = X`. Templates show or hide controls using the same predicates (`can_manage_office`, `can_change_booking`), never their own logic.

### AD-8 — Attendees filtered at the service

- **Binds:** R15
- **Prevents:** the rooms grid, the details panel and the calendar showing attendees to different people
- **Rule:** `bookings.service` returns booking views for a viewer. `attendees` is filled only when the viewer is the organiser, an attendee, or an office manager of the room's office, and is empty otherwise. Templates never load attendees themselves.

### AD-9 — People and offices come only from the seed file

- **Binds:** R1, the user's 2026-11-12 seed decision
- **Prevents:** reloading HR's list changing `people.id`, which would break cookies and bookings; a second import path
- **Rule:** `python -m roombooker.seed <file.csv>` upserts offices and people, keyed on the person's email `[ASSUMPTION]`. A person missing from a later file is marked `active = false`, never deleted `[ASSUMPTION]`. The build seed file and HR's list use the same command and format.

### AD-10 — Schema changes only through migrations

- **Binds:** all epics
- **Prevents:** schema drift between environments; the AD-4 triggers going missing
- **Rule:** every table, index, check and trigger is created by an Alembic migration. `alembic upgrade head` runs as a deploy step before the app starts. Nothing calls `create_all` outside tests.

### AD-11 — One instance, one host, private reach

- **Binds:** OQ-4, RULE-7, RULE-9, the initiative's Done when
- **Prevents:** a second app instance or network storage corrupting SQLite; losing the database; staff names reachable from the internet with no sign-in
- **Rule:**
  - Exactly one app container runs, on one host, with the SQLite file on a local persistent volume.
  - SQLite runs with `journal_mode=WAL`, `busy_timeout=5000` and `foreign_keys=ON`.
  - Caddy terminates HTTPS in front of the app.
  - Litestream replicates the database continuously to object storage off the host.
  - Only company networks (office Wi-Fi and VPN) can reach the app `[ASSUMPTION]`.
  - The host is a small Linux VM in a UK region, run by the company or in the cloud `[ASSUMPTION]`.

### AD-12 — One error path

- **Binds:** R8, R11, all forms
- **Prevents:** each route inventing its own error shape and wording
- **Rule:** services raise `BookingConflict`, `RoomClosed`, `NotAllowed` or `InvalidBooking`. One handler in `core` maps them to 409, 409, 403 and 422 and renders the message fragment in the EXPERIENCE.md voice, inside an `aria-live` region.

### AD-13 — Cancelling deletes `[ASSUMPTION]`

- **Binds:** R11, R12, R13
- **Prevents:** epic-my-calendar having to know about a "cancelled" state invented in epic-find-and-book
- **Rule:** cancelling deletes the booking and its `booking_attendees` rows. `bookings` has no status column. Revisit when OQ-3 (retention) is answered.

## Consistency Conventions

| Concern | Convention |
| --- | --- |
| Naming | Package `roombooker`; tables plural `snake_case`; route paths `/rooms`, `/my-bookings`, `/manage-rooms`, `/bookings/{id}`, `/pick-name` |
| IDs | Integer primary keys; `people.email` is the external key |
| Dates on screen | `14:00`, `Tue 17 Nov`, 24-hour UK time, through Jinja filters in `core/time.py` only |
| Writes | HTML form `POST` only, including change and cancel (`POST /bookings/{id}/cancel`); fragment responses for htmx requests, redirect-after-post otherwise |
| Styling | DESIGN.md tokens as CSS custom properties in `static/tokens.css`; no CSS framework `[ASSUMPTION]` |
| Config | Environment variables read in `core/settings.py` only (`ROOMBOOKER_DB_PATH`, `ROOMBOOKER_ENV`) |
| Logging | stdlib `logging` to stdout; every write logs the acting `person_id`, the action and the target id (evidence for SM-5) |
| Tests | pytest with FastAPI `TestClient` against a temporary SQLite file migrated to head; a concurrency test proves AD-4 |

## Stack

| Name | Version |
| --- | --- |
| Python | 3.14 |
| FastAPI | 0.162.5 |
| Uvicorn | 0.54.0 |
| Jinja2 | 3.1.6 |
| python-multipart | 0.0.33 |
| SQLAlchemy | 2.1.8 |
| Alembic | 1.20.1 |
| SQLite | bundled with Python |
| htmx | 2.0.11 |
| pytest | 9.2.0 |
| httpx | 0.28.1 |
| uv | project and dependency manager |
| Caddy | 2.x, exact version pinned at the deployment story (unverified) |
| Litestream | exact version pinned at the deployment story (unverified) |

## Structural Seed

```mermaid
erDiagram
    offices ||--o{ people : "home office of"
    offices ||--o{ rooms : has
    rooms ||--o{ bookings : "booked as"
    people ||--o{ bookings : organises
    bookings ||--o{ booking_attendees : lists
    people ||--o{ booking_attendees : attends
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph company["Company networks: office Wi-Fi, VPN"]
        L[Laptop browser]
        P[Phone browser]
    end
    subgraph host["One Linux VM, UK region"]
        C[Caddy, HTTPS]
        A[roombooker container, Uvicorn]
        V[(Volume: roombooker.db, WAL)]
        LS[Litestream]
    end
    O[(Off-host object storage)]
    L --> C
    P --> C
    C --> A
    A --> V
    LS --> V
    LS --> O
```

| Environment | What runs | Data |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Local | `uv run uvicorn`, SQLite file in the repo's ignored `var/` | build seed file |
| Production | AD-11 host | build seed before go-live (office managers enter rooms), then HR's list loaded with the same command |

```text
roombooker/
  core/          # settings, db session, current_person, errors, time
  people/        # web, service, store; pick your name
  rooms/         # web, service, store; manage rooms
  bookings/      # web, service, store; rooms view, booking sheet, details panel
  calendar/      # web, service; my bookings
  seed.py        # CLI for AD-9
  templates/     # base.html shell, one folder per module
  static/        # tokens.css, app.css, htmx.min.js
migrations/      # Alembic, including AD-4 triggers
tests/
deploy/          # Dockerfile, Caddyfile, litestream.yml
```

## Capability → Architecture Map

| Capability / Area | Lives in | Governed by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1, R2 pick and switch name | `people`, `core.current_person` | AD-6, AD-9 |
| R3, R4 add and edit rooms | `rooms` | AD-3, AD-7 |
| R5 close and reopen (room side) | `rooms` | AD-7 |
| R5 refuse bookings of a closed room | `bookings`, trigger | AD-4 |
| R6 free rooms by office, date, time, length | `bookings.service` (reads `rooms`) | AD-1, AD-5, RULE-8 |
| R7 book with attendees (making it) | `bookings` | AD-4, AD-5, AD-12 |
| R7 shows in organiser's and attendees' calendars | `calendar` via `bookings.service` | AD-3, AD-8 |
| R8 overlap refused | trigger, `bookings.service` | AD-4, AD-12 |
| R9, R10, R11 change and cancel | `bookings` | AD-4, AD-7, AD-13 |
| R12, R13, R14 my calendar | `calendar` | AD-3, AD-5, AD-7 |
| R15 attendee visibility | `bookings.service` | AD-8 |
| R16 three taps, no typing | `bookings.web` templates | AD-2 |
| RULE-8 under 10 seconds | server-rendered first paint | AD-2 |
| Hosting (OQ-4) | `deploy/` | AD-11 |

## Deferred

- **The fate of a closed room's future bookings:** decided when epic-find-and-book is refined. The AD-4 trigger allows deleting them or moving them to an open room.
- **The exact hosting provider and network restriction:** the user decides with IT. This blocks epic 1's deployment story, not its other stories.
- **Retention of past bookings and attendee lists (OQ-3):** answered before go-live, and may revisit AD-13 or add a purge job.
- **HR file column names:** confirmed with HR. The seed format adapts, and AD-9's email key holds.
- **CI provider, browser end-to-end tool, and monitoring beyond logs and Litestream:** chosen in epic 1's baseline stories.
- **A staging environment:** none planned. Production before go-live is the rehearsal.

- (requirement) R10 (FR-10): an office manager changes any booking of a room in their office under the same rules.
- (requirement) R11 (FR-11): the organiser or an office manager of the room's office cancels a booking; the room is free at once for everyone.
- (requirement) R12 (FR-12): a person sees their own bookings, organised and attended (A4), in a built-in calendar by day and by week.
- (requirement) R13 (FR-13): from the calendar a person opens one of their bookings and changes or cancels it when RULE-3 allows.
- (requirement) R14 (FR-14): a person moves to the previous or next day or week.

10	
11	# Company Room Booking: Experience Spine
12	
13	## Foundation
14	
15	Responsive web app, one surface used on laptops and phones. No UI kit named: plain HTML and CSS served by the app [ASSUMPTION: the architecture decides how pages are rendered]. `DESIGN.md` is the visual identity reference; this spine is the experience.
16	
17	Release one has no login (PRD RULE-6). A person picks their name once, and the app remembers it on that device (PRD FR-2, A2). The current person's name is always visible in the top bar. English only, no dark mode, UK time with 24-hour clock [ASSUMPTION].
18	
19	## Information Architecture
20	
21	| Surface | Reached from | Purpose | PRD |
22	|---|---|---|---|
23	| Pick your name | First visit on a device; top bar name | Choose who you are from the loaded people | FR-1, FR-2 |
24	| Rooms (main screen) | App open; "Rooms" tab | Today's rooms in my office, free and booked. Laptop: day grid. Phone: next free rooms as a list | FR-6 |
25	| Booking sheet | Tapping a free slot or a room row's "Book" | Make a booking in three taps or fewer | FR-7, FR-8 |
26	| Booking details | Tapping any booking (grid, list, calendar) | See title and organiser; change or cancel when allowed | FR-9, FR-10, FR-11, FR-13 |
27	| My bookings | "My bookings" tab | My own calendar, by day and by week | FR-12, FR-14 |
28	| Manage rooms | "Manage rooms" tab, office managers only | Add, edit, close and reopen my office's rooms | FR-3, FR-4, FR-5 |
29	
30	Navigation: tabs in the top bar (Rooms · My bookings · Manage rooms). "Manage rooms" appears only for office managers. Sheets and panels stack one level deep, never two.
31	
32	Closure: every PRD capability FR-1 to FR-14 has a surface, and every surface is reached by a Key Flow below.
33	
34	## Booking Visibility
35	
36	Settles PRD OQ-2 (user): **anyone can see a booking's title and who booked it.** It's an internal tool.
37	
38	| Detail | Who sees it |
39	|---|---|
40	| Room is taken, time, title, organiser | Everyone |
41	| Attendees | The organiser, the attendees, and office managers of the room's office |
42	
43	## Voice and Tone
44	
45	Microcopy. Brand posture lives in `DESIGN.md`.
46	
47	| Do | Don't |
48	|---|---|
49	| "Booked. Atlas, 14:00–14:30." | "Your booking was created successfully!" |
50	| "Someone just booked Atlas at 14:00. These rooms are still free:" | "Error 409: conflict" |
51	| "Free until 15:30" | "Available for the next 90 minutes" |
52	| "Closed" | "Unavailable (room status: inactive)" |
53	| "No bookings this week." | "Looks like you have nothing planned! 🎉" |
54	| Times as 14:00, dates as "Tue 17 Nov" [ASSUMPTION] | 2pm, 11/17 |
55	
56	Short, plain, no exclamation marks. Name the room and the time in every confirmation.
57	
58	## Component Patterns
59	
60	Behavioral. Visual specs live in `DESIGN.md.Components`.
61	
62	| Component | Use | Behavioral rules |
63	|---|---|---|
64	| Name picker | Pick your name | Type-ahead search over all ~300 people; shows name and home office. Picking sets the current person on this device and opens Rooms. |
65	| Office switcher | Rooms | Defaults to my home office. Switching shows that office's rooms; the choice lasts for the visit, then resets to home [ASSUMPTION]. |
66	| Date switcher | Rooms, My bookings | Today by default; previous/next day; "Today" button returns. |
67	| Day grid | Rooms, laptop | One row per room, time across in 15-minute columns from 07:00 to 20:00. Tapping a free slot opens the booking sheet with that room and start time. Tapping a booked slot opens booking details. |
68	| Next free rooms list | Rooms, phone | Rooms in my office free from the next quarter-hour, each with "Free until …" and a "Book" button; free-now rooms first, then by soonest free [ASSUMPTION]. Rooms already taken for the next hour sit below a "Busy now" heading; closed rooms are hidden from the list [ASSUMPTION]. A length choice (30 min / 1 h / 2 h) filters to rooms free for that long [ASSUMPTION]. |
69	| Booking sheet | From a slot or room row | Room, start time and length prefilled (length defaults to 30 minutes). Title prefilled as "{Name}'s meeting" and editable, so booking needs no typing. Attendees optional, picked by type-ahead. Length: 15 min to 4 h in 15-minute steps (PRD RULE-2). "Book" is the only primary action. |
70	| Booking details | From any booking | Shows room, time, title, organiser (attendees per Booking Visibility). "Change" and "Cancel booking" appear only when PRD RULE-3 allows: organiser, or an office manager of the room's office. "Cancel booking" asks once for confirmation [ASSUMPTION]. |
71	| My bookings calendar | My bookings | Day and week toggle. Shows bookings I organise and bookings I attend (PRD FR-12, A4), each marked "Organiser" or "Attending". Previous/next day or week. |
72	| Rooms table | Manage rooms | My office's rooms: name, capacity, status (Open/Closed). "Add room", and per row "Edit" and "Close" / "Reopen". Closing asks for confirmation and says how many future bookings the room has; what happens to them is decided in the epic (PRD FR-5). |
73	
74	## State Patterns
75	
76	| State | Surface | Treatment |
77	|---|---|---|
78	| No name picked on this device | Any | Open Pick your name first; return to the requested surface after. |
79	| Slot taken a moment earlier | Booking sheet | Booking refused (PRD FR-8). Error message above "Book": "Someone just booked {room} at {time}. These rooms are still free:" with up to three free rooms for the same time, each one tap to book. The sheet keeps title and attendees. |
80	| Change would overlap | Booking details | Same refusal message; the original booking is unchanged. |
81	| Room closed | Day grid | Row in closed style with "Closed"; no slots tappable. Hidden from the phone list. |
82	| Past times | Day grid | Slots before now are greyed and not tappable [ASSUMPTION]. |
83	| No free rooms | Phone list | "No rooms free in {office} for {length} from {time}." Offer the next time any room is free, and the office switcher. |
84	| Empty calendar | My bookings | "No bookings today." / "No bookings this week." |
85	| Not an office manager | Manage rooms | Tab hidden; a direct link shows "Only office managers can manage rooms." |
86	| Save failed (network) | Any form | Error message: "Couldn't save. Check your connection and try again." Form keeps its values. |
87	| Loading | Rooms, My bookings | Grid or list outline appears at once; content fills in. Free rooms within the 10-second target (PRD RULE-8). |
88	
89	## Interaction Primitives
90	
91	- **Tap or click** to act. No drag, no swipe gestures, no long-press in release one [ASSUMPTION].
92	- **Three taps or fewer to book (user):** laptop: tap a free slot → "Book" (2 taps). Phone: "Book" on a room row → "Book" (2 taps). Changing length, title or attendees is optional and adds taps only when wanted.
93	- **Times snap to 15 minutes** in every picker (PRD RULE-2).
94	- **Keyboard:** Tab moves through controls in reading order; Enter activates; Esc closes the booking sheet or details panel.
95	- **Banned:** sheets on top of sheets; hover-only actions; confirmation dialogs for booking (refusal handles conflicts); auto-refreshing the grid under the user's finger.
96	
97	## Accessibility Floor
98	
99	Behavioral. Visual contrast lives in `DESIGN.md` (white on navy and ink-muted on white both meet AA).
100	
101	- WCAG 2.2 AA across laptop and phone [ASSUMPTION].
102	- Slot and room state is always in words ("Free", "Booked: {title}, {organiser}", "Closed"), never color alone.
103	- The day grid is a real table: room names as row headers, times as column headers, so screen readers announce "Atlas, 14:00, Free".
104	- Every tap target is at least 44px.
105	- Booking results and refusals are announced through a live region.
106	- Focus moves into the booking sheet when it opens and back to the tapped slot or row when it closes.
107	
108	## Responsive & Platform
109	
110	| Width | Rooms | My bookings | Booking sheet |
111	|---|---|---|---|
112	| ≥ 768px (laptop) | Day grid, all rooms visible | Week grid or day column | Centred panel |
113	| < 768px (phone) | Next free rooms list, not a calendar (user) | Day list by default; week as seven day-headed lists [ASSUMPTION] | Bottom sheet |
114	
115	Tabs stay in the top bar at every width [ASSUMPTION]. Manage rooms works on phone as a simple list, but is designed laptop-first [ASSUMPTION].
116	
117	## Key Flows
118

# Company Room Booking: Experience Spine

## Foundation

Responsive web app, one surface used on laptops and phones. No UI kit named: plain HTML and CSS served by the app [ASSUMPTION: the architecture decides how pages are rendered]. `DESIGN.md` is the visual identity reference; this spine is the experience.

Release one has no login (PRD RULE-6). A person picks their name once, and the app remembers it on that device (PRD FR-2, A2). The current person's name is always visible in the top bar. English only, no dark mode, UK time with 24-hour clock [ASSUMPTION].

## Information Architecture

| Surface | Reached from | Purpose | PRD |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pick your name | First visit on a device; top bar name | Choose who you are from the loaded people | FR-1, FR-2 |
| Rooms (main screen) | App open; "Rooms" tab | Today's rooms in my office, free and booked. Laptop: day grid. Phone: next free rooms as a list | FR-6 |
| Booking sheet | Tapping a free slot or a room row's "Book" | Make a booking in three taps or fewer | FR-7, FR-8 |
| Booking details | Tapping any booking (grid, list, calendar) | See title and organiser; change or cancel when allowed | FR-9, FR-10, FR-11, FR-13 |
| My bookings | "My bookings" tab | My own calendar, by day and by week | FR-12, FR-14 |
| Manage rooms | "Manage rooms" tab, office managers only | Add, edit, close and reopen my office's rooms | FR-3, FR-4, FR-5 |

Navigation: tabs in the top bar (Rooms · My bookings · Manage rooms). "Manage rooms" appears only for office managers. Sheets and panels stack one level deep, never two.

Closure: every PRD capability FR-1 to FR-14 has a surface, and every surface is reached by a Key Flow below.

## Booking Visibility

Settles PRD OQ-2 (user): **anyone can see a booking's title and who booked it.** It's an internal tool.

| Detail | Who sees it |
|---|---|
| Room is taken, time, title, organiser | Everyone |
| Attendees | The organiser, the attendees, and office managers of the room's office |

## Voice and Tone

Microcopy. Brand posture lives in `DESIGN.md`.

| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| "Booked. Atlas, 14:00–14:30." | "Your booking was created successfully!" |
| "Someone just booked Atlas at 14:00. These rooms are still free:" | "Error 409: conflict" |
| "Free until 15:30" | "Available for the next 90 minutes" |
| "Closed" | "Unavailable (room status: inactive)" |
| "No bookings this week." | "Looks like you have nothing planned! 🎉" |
| Times as 14:00, dates as "Tue 17 Nov" [ASSUMPTION] | 2pm, 11/17 |

Short, plain, no exclamation marks. Name the room and the time in every confirmation.

## Component Patterns

Behavioral. Visual specs live in `DESIGN.md.Components`.

| Component | Use | Behavioral rules |
|---|---|---|
| Name picker | Pick your name | Type-ahead search over all ~300 people; shows name and home office. Picking sets the current person on this device and opens Rooms. |
| Office switcher | Rooms | Defaults to my home office. Switching shows that office's rooms; the choice lasts for the visit, then resets to home [ASSUMPTION]. |
| Date switcher | Rooms, My bookings | Today by default; previous/next day; "Today" button returns. |
| Day grid | Rooms, laptop | One row per room, time across in 15-minute columns from 07:00 to 20:00. Tapping a free slot opens the booking sheet with that room and start time. Tapping a booked slot opens booking details. |
| Next free rooms list | Rooms, phone | Rooms in my office free from the next quarter-hour, each with "Free until …" and a "Book" button; free-now rooms first, then by soonest free [ASSUMPTION]. Rooms already taken for the next hour sit below a "Busy now" heading; closed rooms are hidden from the list [ASSUMPTION]. A length choice (30 min / 1 h / 2 h) filters to rooms free for that long [ASSUMPTION]. |
| Booking sheet | From a slot or room row | Room, start time and length prefilled (length defaults to 30 minutes). Title prefilled as "{Name}'s meeting" and editable, so booking needs no typing. Attendees optional, picked by type-ahead. Length: 15 min to 4 h in 15-minute steps (PRD RULE-2). "Book" is the only primary action. |
| Booking details | From any booking | Shows room, time, title, organiser (attendees per Booking Visibility). "Change" and "Cancel booking" appear only when PRD RULE-3 allows: organiser, or an office manager of the room's office. "Cancel booking" asks once for confirmation [ASSUMPTION]. |
| My bookings calendar | My bookings | Day and week toggle. Shows bookings I organise and bookings I attend (PRD FR-12, A4), each marked "Organiser" or "Attending". Previous/next day or week. |
| Rooms table | Manage rooms | My office's rooms: name, capacity, status (Open/Closed). "Add room", and per row "Edit" and "Close" / "Reopen". Closing asks for confirmation and says how many future bookings the room has; what happens to them is decided in the epic (PRD FR-5). |

## State Patterns

| State | Surface | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| No name picked on this device | Any | Open Pick your name first; return to the requested surface after. |
| Slot taken a moment earlier | Booking sheet | Booking refused (PRD FR-8). Error message above "Book": "Someone just booked {room} at {time}. These rooms are still free:" with up to three free rooms for the same time, each one tap to book. The sheet keeps title and attendees. |
| Change would overlap | Booking details | Same refusal message; the original booking is unchanged. |
| Room closed | Day grid | Row in closed style with "Closed"; no slots tappable. Hidden from the phone list. |
| Past times | Day grid | Slots before now are greyed and not tappable [ASSUMPTION]. |
| No free rooms | Phone list | "No rooms free in {office} for {length} from {time}." Offer the next time any room is free, and the office switcher. |
| Empty calendar | My bookings | "No bookings today." / "No bookings this week." |
| Not an office manager | Manage rooms | Tab hidden; a direct link shows "Only office managers can manage rooms." |
| Save failed (network) | Any form | Error message: "Couldn't save. Check your connection and try again." Form keeps its values. |
| Loading | Rooms, My bookings | Grid or list outline appears at once; content fills in. Free rooms within the 10-second target (PRD RULE-8). |

## Interaction Primitives

- **Tap or click** to act. No drag, no swipe gestures, no long-press in release one [ASSUMPTION].
- **Three taps or fewer to book (user):** laptop: tap a free slot → "Book" (2 taps). Phone: "Book" on a room row → "Book" (2 taps). Changing length, title or attendees is optional and adds taps only when wanted.
- **Times snap to 15 minutes** in every picker (PRD RULE-2).
- **Keyboard:** Tab moves through controls in reading order; Enter activates; Esc closes the booking sheet or details panel.
- **Banned:** sheets on top of sheets; hover-only actions; confirmation dialogs for booking (refusal handles conflicts); auto-refreshing the grid under the user's finger.

## Accessibility Floor

Behavioral. Visual contrast lives in `DESIGN.md` (white on navy and ink-muted on white both meet AA).

- WCAG 2.2 AA across laptop and phone [ASSUMPTION].
- Slot and room state is always in words ("Free", "Booked: {title}, {organiser}", "Closed"), never color alone.
- The day grid is a real table: room names as row headers, times as column headers, so screen readers announce "Atlas, 14:00, Free".
- Every tap target is at least 44px.
- Booking results and refusals are announced through a live region.
- Focus moves into the booking sheet when it opens and back to the tapped slot or row when it closes.

## Responsive & Platform

| Width | Rooms | My bookings | Booking sheet |
|---|---|---|---|
| ≥ 768px (laptop) | Day grid, all rooms visible | Week grid or day column | Centred panel |
| < 768px (phone) | Next free rooms list, not a calendar (user) | Day list by default; week as seven day-headed lists [ASSUMPTION] | Bottom sheet |

Tabs stay in the top bar at every width [ASSUMPTION]. Manage rooms works on phone as a simple list, but is designed laptop-first [ASSUMPTION].

## Key Flows

Journey names mirror the PRD. Protagonists are roles, because no real session was narrated [ASSUMPTION, PRD A1].

### UJ-1: A Leeds staff member books a room for this afternoon

1. Opens the app on their phone. It remembers their name, so Rooms opens on Leeds, today.
2. The next free rooms list shows rooms free from 14:00. They choose "1 h".
3. They tap "Book" on a room showing "Free until 16:00".
4. The booking sheet opens with room, 14:00–15:00 and "{Name}'s meeting" filled in. They add two colleagues as attendees.
5. **Climax:** they tap "Book". "Booked. {Room}, 14:00–15:00." The booking appears in their My bookings and in both attendees' calendars. Two taps, plus the attendees they chose to add.

Failure: someone booked that room a moment earlier. The sheet shows the refusal and three rooms still free at 14:00; one tap books another.

### UJ-2: A Manchester staff member books a room in London for a visit

1. On their laptop, Rooms opens on Manchester. They switch the office to London and the date to next Tuesday.
2. The day grid shows London's rooms; they tap a free slot at 10:00.
3. In the sheet they set the length to 2 h and add London colleagues.
4. **Climax:** "Book". The slot turns solid navy, with their title on it, in London's grid.

### UJ-3: An organiser moves and cancels meetings

1. They open My bookings, week view.
2. They tap a meeting; details show "Change" and "Cancel booking".
3. "Change": they move it to Thursday 11:00; the app checks the room is free and saves.
4. They open another meeting and tap "Cancel booking", then confirm.
5. **Climax:** the week view updates at once; the cancelled room shows as free in Rooms for everyone.

### UJ-4: A London office manager closes a room for repairs

1. They open Manage rooms; the table lists London's rooms.
2. "Close" on a room: the confirmation says it has 3 future bookings and that closing stops new bookings.
3. They confirm; the room shows "Closed" in the grid. Later they "Add room" for a newly fitted room.
4. From the Rooms grid they tap someone's booking in a London room; as an office manager they see "Change" and "Cancel booking" and move it to free the slot for an urgent meeting.
5. **Climax:** the grid shows the closed room greyed out, the new room open, and the urgent slot free. The room list matches reality.

## Open items

- What happens to future bookings when a room closes is decided in the rooms epic (PRD FR-5); the UX only shows the count.
- Exact company navy and any logo: to be supplied; DESIGN.md hex values stand until then.

🎯 I'm Sofia, the Product Owner. I've read epic 1 (`epic-offices-and-rooms`), the five initiative requirements it covers (R1–R5), the architecture spine, and the UX. There's no code in the repo yet beyond the README. You can call in `bmad-party-mode` for more points of view or `bmad-advanced-elicitation` to push harder at any point.

## Already settled for this epic's stories

- **Stack and layout:** the spine fixes the stack and versions (Python 3.14, FastAPI, SQLite, Alembic, htmx), the package layout and the naming. Every table, index and trigger comes from a migration (AD-10).
- **Current person:** a 400-day unsigned `person_id` cookie. A missing cookie, or one naming an unknown or inactive person, sends you to Pick your name and then back where you were going (AD-6).
- **Office manager:** someone with the office-manager mark whose home office is that office. The check is made in the service layer and refuses with "not allowed" (AD-7).
- **Seed load:** `python -m roombooker.seed <file.csv>` adds and updates people and offices, matched on email. Anyone missing from a later file is marked inactive, not deleted (AD-9).
- **Errors and logging:** one error path (AD-12). Every change logs who did it, what they did and to what, as evidence for SM-5.
- **Screens:** the name picker (type-ahead, name and home office) and the rooms table (name, capacity, Open/Closed, Add, Edit, Close/Reopen) come from EXPERIENCE. Manage rooms is laptop-first and a simple list on phone. Anyone else sees "Only office managers can manage rooms."
- **Hosting shape:** one container on one UK-region VM, with Caddy for HTTPS and Litestream for backups (AD-11).
- **Close:** it only marks the room closed. The future-booking count and what happens to those bookings belong to epic 2.

## Still open — my pick for each

1. **Hosting provider and network restriction (OQ-4).** I'd leave this open and split deployment in two:
   - **A deploy bundle** (Dockerfile, Caddyfile, Litestream config) that runs locally. It isn't blocked by the question.
   - **Standing it up on the company host.** This needs a person, so it's a manual step, and it's blocked until OQ-4 is answered.

   The epic's Done when says "on the deployed app", so the epic can't close until you and IT answer. *Do you already know the provider?*
2. **Seed file format.** I'd settle this now. Columns: `email, name, office, office_manager`. Office is written by name (London, Manchester, Leeds), and the load creates offices from what it finds. I'd add a made-up build seed of about 30 people across the three offices. The column names change when HR confirms theirs (spine: Deferred); matching on email stays.
3. **Room rules.** I'd settle these now:
   - A room has a name and a capacity, a whole number of 1 or more.
   - Names are unique within an office.
   - Edit changes the name and capacity only; open or closed changes only through Close and Reopen.
4. **What a person sees before epic 2 ships Rooms.** I'd settle this now. Tabs appear only once their screen exists.
   - Office managers land on Manage rooms.
   - Everyone else lands on a short page with their name and "Booking opens soon." Epic 2 replaces it.

   This matches the rollout, where only office managers use the app before go-live.
5. **CI and the browser test tool.** The spine leaves both to this epic.
   - **Browser tests:** I'd settle on Playwright for Python now, to run the laptop and phone checks in the integrated verification.
   - **CI:** the repo has no remote yet, so I'd leave CI to the scaffold story and keep `uv run pytest` as the check until then. *Where will the code be hosted?*

**Left to the stories:** wording of validation messages, a capacity ceiling, and how picker search behaves.

**No spike needed.** Nothing here can only be answered by writing code.

## If you want more depth first

You can flesh the epic out before I write it up:
- your own notes;
- a document from John (`bmad-agent-pm`) on the epic;
- `bmad-ux` or `bmad-architecture` run on the epic;
- research with `bmad-deep-recon`.

None of these seem needed to me: the spine and UX already cover this epic well.

Say yes to my picks, or change any of them. Answers on 1 and 5 would help too. Then I'll write the epic's requirements, mark it refined and commit.

# Requirements

Turns any intent input into a container's **derived lines**: the Requirements and Constraints sections and the `Assumption:` and `Open question:` lines, plus its companions.



## Workspace

The workspace is the ticket the user or the calling capability names, else the active initiative; a ticket named by id or title resolves as Dispatch in `workflow.md` says. A ticket with no file yet is created first from `/home/claude/runs/room-booker/_bmad/render/bmad-agent-po/room-booker-72ea137e33d5/29ecc89ff22a7f491c6e/assets/ticket-template.md`; at create SPEC also fills Description, Outcome, Done when (three to six checks at the altitude of the source's ids), Boundaries (the input's non-goals) and References from the input, open questions to Notes; a later slice revises them. A new initiative, named from the input's title, is created and recorded as On activation in `workflow.md` says.

**No input.** Ask for a file path, pasted content, an explanation, or a source.

## Memory and derivation

`.memlog.md` is append-only, one line per entry; requirements carry their stable `R<n>`. Each run derives the derived lines and every spec-authored companion from the memlog plus the sources it cites.

On a container, SPEC is the only writer of the derived lines; a change goes to the memlog, never into them by hand. A derive replaces exactly those lines, sets `sources:` and `companions:` in the frontmatter, adds a References line per companion, and touches nothing else. A source id on a line must exist in a `sources:` file; neither list names the memlog, README files or process records.

- **A container's** `status` is Sofia's to edit in its file: absent until its first ticket starts, then `in-progress`, then `done` or `dropped` on the user's confirmation; a published one transitions through `write`.

## Close, drop, move

- Closing every child does not close the parent. Run the closure check in `validate.md` against its requirements and Done when; the user confirms completion.
- Drop only after a `Dropped:` line in the ticket's Notes, or its epic's when it has no file, says why; then set `dropped` per Status, or on a tracker an unpublished entry takes `tracker_status: dropped` through `mirror`. Never delete an entry from an approved `tickets.toml`. With the user, remove or repoint the dropped ticket in each dependent's `after` (`status` lists them under `blocks`). Cancelling a container cancels its descendants once the user confirms.
- Move an entry with `tickets.py move`; it renumbers the entry, moves its file and plan, rewrites every `after` naming it, and reports what it rewrote. It lands last in the destination's `tickets.toml`; put it in build order by hand. Move its `covers` ids between the two epics with the user if the requirement moves. An epic moves as its whole folder with its `[[epic]]` table. Then run `tickets.py status` on the initiative and clear what it reports.
- A done standalone ticket stays in `backlog/` beside its plan.

## Tracker sync

After every `write`, and after the `query` before a board view, run `tickets.py mirror [<folder>]` with a JSON array on stdin, one object per ticket: `ref` (or its `tracker_id`) plus any of `tracker_id`, `remote`, `tracker_status`, `assignee`, `after`.

- `tracker_status` is the state mapped back through `[tickets.status]`: after `write`, the state sent; when two states share a tracker status the query cannot tell apart, the current one if it matches, else the earlier.
- `after` holds tracker ids as strings; an empty string removes a key's line.
- A tracker leaf missing from the tree, even one a known ticket's `after` names, comes back under `unmatched`: add an `[[entry]]` to the parent's `tickets.toml` (the folder's `next_id`, the item's type and title, a one-sentence description), mirror again with that `ref`, and put the item's body in the pulled file.
- Query published containers with their leaves; `mirror` reports them under `containers`, never `unmatched`; tell the user when one's tracker status differs from its file's, and close one only through the closure check.
- A body that differs from the file: show both and ask.
- Move a ticket the tracker shows under another parent per Close, drop, move, then mirror again.
- A failed store call: tell the user what blocks it, confirm the setup, and ask them to authenticate if that is the cause. An empty verb field you cannot infer: ask, and offer to record it per `store-setup.md`.


=====TEMPLATE

tracker_id: ""   # with remote (url): set at publish on a tracker, on a story by `tickets.py mirror`; cut on the repo store
id: [story: its tickets.toml entry id, or the folder's `next_id` if none; cut on a container]
type: [initiative | epic | story]
title: "[Container: its outcome. Story: what works when done]"
parent: [the parent container's folder name; none for an initiative or a backlog/ story]
covers: [epic: parent ids it owns; story: epic ids it serves; cut on an initiative. Constraints go in References, not here]
sources: []   # every input SPEC derived Requirements from, paths from {project-root}; each is re-read on update; never the memlog
companions: []   # files downstream reads beside this ticket, written or adopted by SPEC, paths from {project-root}
after: []   # container: epics it waits on; epic order is in tickets.toml. Story: prerequisites only: sibling id, "<epic id>.<entry id>", or epic-<slug>
assignee: ""   # story: only a tracker's, via `tickets.py mirror`; cut on a container
# container: add status: in-progress | done | dropped when its first ticket starts
# a story's status, assignee, blocked_at, blocked_reason live in the plan beside this file, not here; tracker_status from tracker sync
refined: false   # story: true once the user approves its criteria; on a pulled story only if its entry has `refine = true`. Epic: false only when slicing writes it thin, until refined; else cut. Cut on an initiative
hitl: false   # true when a person does part of the work; story only, cut on a container
risk: [low|medium|high; container: a best guess until sliced, then its children's highest]
---

<!-- At create a container gets all but Requirements and Constraints, which SPEC writes from an input. An epic written at slicing gets Description, Outcome, Boundaries, Done when as far as known, and References to the parent; Requirements and Constraints come when it is refined. A pulled or reviewed story: Description, Verify: line, References, local Notes; refining adds numbered criteria and Boundaries. Done and dropped tickets stay as written. An initiative is the business outcome its epics serve, usually spanning quarters and more than one boundary; for a solo developer or small team a whole product is a fine initiative. -->

# [Title]

## Description

[Container: a paragraph, what is true when done and why, pointing at the inputs or parent. Story: one sentence; with numbered criteria, 2–4 on how it advances the epic, not restating them.]

## Outcome

[Container: one sentence: for whom, what changes, the source's success signal named not restated. Story: cut.]

## Requirements

[Container: SPEC writes this from the ticket's `.memlog.md`; slicing never touches it. Initiative: `R<n> (<source ids>): <checkable result>`, ids prefixed with the source's References type when ambiguous (`prd FR-2`), its section when it has none. Epic: its owned parent lines, `R<n> (parent R<m>): <the line>`, deepened only as inputs require; split or added lines name a parent id or source section, all lines a source section when `covers` is empty. Story: only `Verify: how it will be checked`. No epic, `refine = true`, or on request: numbered criteria, each naming the epic ids it proves; a criterion states a rule, not an instance, with its failure path.]

1. **[Behavior name]** (R<m>)
   **Given** [state before]
   **When** [the one action]
   **Then** [what is observable]
   **And** [another observation, if any]

## Constraints

[SPEC writes this. Initiative: each design-bending non-negotiable, citing its source id or section. Epic: the parent's that bind it. Story: only ones beyond its epic's; behavior to keep goes under Boundaries.]

## Done when

[Container: three to six end checks from the source's measures and limits: an initiative's business outcomes, an epic's deliverables at its Requirements' altitude, production delivery among them. Story: cut.]

## Boundaries

[Container: its boundary and what it is not, from the source's non-goals. Initiative: plus a line per touched unit with no epic, and a one-sentence tracer path across epics. Epic: what belongs to siblings. Story: with numbered criteria, adjacent behavior an implementation could break, not files; else cut.]

- Touch point: [unit] — [what is used there]; owner: epic-[slug]
- Must not change: [behavior]

## References

[`type — location, section`, location a path from {project-root} or a url. A line per companion SPEC writes or adopts, typed by content (glossary, design, architecture, prd). Initiative: section pointers into its sources and companions. Epic: the parent's Requirements, then the architecture spine section and design it adopts. Story: the parent, plus what the epic's lack.]

- parent — [path or url, section Requirements]
- [companion — a file beside this one, named for its content]
- [design — an adopted companion, such as DESIGN.md in the ux-<slug>/ run beside this file, or a url]

## Notes

[Only what is unsettled here and not in the repo or source, one marked line each; cut if empty. SPEC writes Assumption: and Open question: from the memlog; slicing and refining, the rest.]

- Assumption: [an unconfirmed choice; once confirmed, a dated Decision]
- Open question: [container: what the source leaves open, and who waits; story: only its own, answered in its work]
- Unknown: [the gap and the entries waiting on it; gates an entry only once copied to its `unknown` key]
- Parked: [an unplaced requirement id, why, with the user's knowledge]
- Decision: [the user's choice, dated; a declined suggestion too]
- Source conflict: [id or section — source vs code or another source]
- Waits on [epic] because: [reason, one per after entry]
- Dropped: [why, before status goes to dropped]

usage: memlog.py [-h] {init,append,set} ...

memlog — an append-only memory log: LLM-optimal working memory for a skill.

A memlog is the dense, chronological record of everything that mattered in a piece of
work — every item the user generated or accepted — kept minimal like human memory: only
what's important, never bloated. It persists ACROSS sessions, so a fresh session can
load it and continue. It is NOT a deliverable; downstream artifacts (a brief, a PRD, a
deck, a report) are *derived* from it on demand. The host skill supplies the vocabulary
by how it calls `append` — the tool stays neutral.

It is a FLAT log: there are no sections or grouping. Every entry is one line, recorded
at the END in the order it happened. The chronology itself is the structure — an event
like "started technique X" is just another entry, same as an idea or an insight.

Three invariants make it trustworthy:

  1. Append-only, chronological. Entries land at the end, in the order they happen.
     Nothing is ever inserted backward, reordered, edited, or removed. There is no
     edit or delete subcommand by design; history is never rewritten.
  2. Write-only / blind. Every command is a context-free write and echoes the new state
     as one line of JSON, so the caller never re-reads the file mid-session. `append` adds
     its line with one OS append write, so concurrent appenders never drop each other.
     The one time the file is read is on resume — and the caller reads it itself, not
     via this script.
  3. No lifecycle status. A memory log has no "complete" flag. Whether the work is done,
     blocked, or paused is itself a fact that happened, so it is recorded as an entry
     (e.g. `append --type event --text "session complete"`), never as frontmatter the
     log would have to mutate. The chronology stays the single source of truth, and a
     resume learns the state by reading the last entries — the same way it learns

# Office managers keep their rooms current

## Description

The deployed app's first release: anyone picks their name from the seeded people, and an office manager adds, edits, closes and reopens their own office's rooms. It lays the ground the later epics build on: the scaffold, the database, seed loading, deployment, the app shell, the type-ahead people picker, the current person and the office-manager check. Office managers can enter and check their rooms on the live app before go-live, as the initiative's rollout asks.

## Outcome

Office managers in London, Manchester and Leeds keep an accurate room list on the deployed app, so the rooms exist before anyone books (initiative R1 to R5).

## Requirements

- R1 (parent R1): A person picks their name from the seeded active people by typing part of it, then uses the app as that person; their name shows in the top bar on every page.
- R2 (parent R2): A person switches name from the top bar at any time; the device remembers the picked name until they switch; a missing, unknown or inactive name opens Pick your name and then returns to the page asked for.
- R3 (parent R3; user 2026-11-12): An office manager adds a room to their office with a name and a capacity; it appears in their rooms table as Open.
- R4 (parent R4; user 2026-11-12): An office manager edits the name and capacity of a room in their office.
- R5 (parent R5): An office manager closes and reopens a room in their office; a closed room shows as Closed and a reopened one as Open.
- R6 (parent RULE-4; experience State Patterns): Anyone who is not an office manager of a room's office is refused adding, editing, closing or reopening its rooms, even by a direct request; the Manage rooms tab shows only to office managers, and a direct link shows "Only office managers can manage rooms."
- R7 (user 2026-11-12): A room with an empty name, a capacity that is not a whole number of 1 or more, or a name already used in its office is refused with the reason, and the form keeps its values.
- R8 (parent Constraints, seed file; user 2026-11-12): One command loads offices, people, home offices and office-manager marks from a CSV with columns `email, name, office, office_manager`; a reload updates people matched on email and marks anyone missing from it inactive, keeping their id; the same command loads the build seed and HR's list.
- R9 (user 2026-11-12): Tabs show only for screens that exist; until epic-find-and-book ships Rooms, after picking a name an office manager lands on Manage rooms and anyone else on a page with their name and "Booking opens soon."

## Constraints

- Parent RULE-4: Only office managers add, edit, close or reopen rooms, and only in their home office.
- Parent RULE-6: No accounts or passwords; anyone can pick anyone's name; every change logs the acting person, as evidence for SM-5.
- Parent RULE-7: Python, FastAPI and SQLite; built and tested on the user's computer; hosted per architecture AD-11.
- Parent RULE-9: Every feature works in a browser on laptop and phone; Manage rooms is laptop-first and a simple list on phone.
- Parent Constraints, Rollout: Office managers check their office's rooms on the live app before go-live, so this epic reaches production before epic-find-and-book.
- User, 2026-11-12: Integrated verification runs with Playwright for Python at laptop and phone widths.

## Done when

- On the deployed app, a person picks their name from the seeded people, the app shows it throughout, and the device remembers it until they switch.
- An office manager adds, edits, closes and reopens rooms in their own office only; anyone else is refused, including by a direct request.
- A closed room shows as Closed; invalid or duplicate rooms are refused with the reason.
- Offices, people, home offices and office-manager marks load from the seed file with one command, and reloading with HR's list keeps everyone's id.
- Integrated verification on the deployed app passes, on laptop and phone.

## Boundaries

- Not here: finding free rooms, bookings, refusing bookings of a closed room, the future-booking count when closing, or what happens to those bookings; all epic-find-and-book.
- Not here: the calendar; epic-my-calendar.
- Not here: editing people or offices inside the app (initiative Boundaries).
- Owns for later epics: the shell (top bar with the current name, tabs, DESIGN.md tokens), the people picker, the current person and the office-manager check.

## References

- parent — _bmad-output/initiative-company-room-booking/initiative-company-room-booking.md, section Requirements (R1 to R5) and Constraints
- architecture — _bmad-output/initiative-company-room-booking/architecture-company-room-booking/architecture-company-room-booking.md, AD-1, AD-2, AD-3, AD-6, AD-7, AD-9, AD-10, AD-11, AD-12, Consistency Conventions, Stack, Structural Seed
- experience — _bmad-output/initiative-company-room-booking/ux-company-room-booking/EXPERIENCE.md, Name picker, Rooms table, State Patterns, Responsive & Platform, UJ-4
- design — _bmad-output/initiative-company-room-booking/ux-company-room-booking/DESIGN.md

## Notes

- Assumption: People are matched on email, and anyone missing from a reload is marked inactive, not deleted (architecture AD-9).
- Assumption: Only company networks reach the app, since there is no sign-in (architecture AD-11); confirmed with OQ-4.
- Open question: Host provider and company-network-only reach (initiative OQ-4). Owner: user with IT. Blocks the host stand-up story and so the epic's close, not its other stories.
- Open question: Where the code is hosted, which decides CI. Owner: user. Blocks CI only; `uv run pytest` is the check until then.
- Open question: HR's column names. Owner: user with HR. Needed before HR's list loads; R8's columns adapt, the email key holds.
- Unknown: OQ-4 gates the story that stands the app up on the company host; it goes on that entry's `unknown` when stories are planned.
- Decision: 2026-11-12, user: opening epic, because nothing can be booked until rooms exist; the platform baseline is its first stories.
- Decision: 2026-11-12, user: deployment splits into a deploy bundle (Dockerfile, Caddyfile, Litestream config) that runs locally, unblocked, and standing it up on the company host, a person's step blocked on OQ-4.
- Decision: 2026-11-12, user: seed CSV columns `email, name, office, office_manager`, office by name; a made-up build seed of about 30 people across the three offices.
- Decision: 2026-11-12, user: a room is a name and a capacity (whole number, 1 or more), names unique within an office; Edit changes only name and capacity, status changes only through Close and Reopen.
- Decision: 2026-11-12, user: tabs appear only once their screen exists; the "Booking opens soon." landing for people who are not office managers is replaced by epic-find-and-book's Rooms.
- Decision: 2026-11-12, user: Playwright for Python for integrated verification; CI is chosen in the scaffold story once the code has a host.
- Decision: 2026-11-12, user: validation wording, a capacity ceiling and picker search behavior are left to the stories; no spike needed.

# Office managers keep their rooms current

## Description

The deployed app's first release: anyone picks their name from the seeded people, and an office manager adds, edits, closes and reopens their own office's rooms. It lays the ground the later epics build on: the scaffold, the database, seed loading, deployment, the app shell, the type-ahead people picker, the current person and the office-manager check. Office managers can enter and check their rooms on the live app before go-live, as the initiative's rollout asks.

## Outcome

Office managers in London, Manchester and Leeds keep an accurate room list on the deployed app, so the rooms exist before anyone books (initiative R1 to R5).

## Requirements

- R1 (parent R1): A person picks their name from the seeded active people by typing part of it, then uses the app as that person; their name shows in the top bar on every page.
- R2 (parent R2): A person switches name from the top bar at any time; the device remembers the picked name until they switch; a missing, unknown or inactive name opens Pick your name and then returns to the page asked for.
- R3 (parent R3; user 2026-11-12): An office manager adds a room to their office with a name and a capacity; it appears in their rooms table as Open.
- R4 (parent R4; user 2026-11-12): An office manager edits the name and capacity of a room in their office.
- R5 (parent R5): An office manager closes and reopens a room in their office; a closed room shows as Closed and a reopened one as Open.
- R6 (parent RULE-4; experience State Patterns): Anyone who is not an office manager of a room's office is refused adding, editing, closing or reopening its rooms, even by a direct request; the Manage rooms tab shows only to office managers, and a direct link shows "Only office managers can manage rooms."
- R7 (user 2026-11-12): A room with an empty name, a capacity that is not a whole number of 1 or more, or a name already used in its office is refused with the reason, and the form keeps its values.
- R8 (parent Constraints, seed file; user 2026-11-12): One command loads offices, people, home offices and office-manager marks from a CSV with columns `email, name, office, office_manager`; a reload updates people matched on email and marks anyone missing from it inactive, keeping their id; the same command loads the build seed and HR's list.
- R9 (user 2026-11-12): Tabs show only for screens that exist; until epic-find-and-book ships Rooms, after picking a name an office manager lands on Manage rooms and anyone else on a page with their name and "Booking opens soon."

## Constraints

- Parent RULE-4: Only office managers add, edit, close or reopen rooms, and only in their home office.
- Parent RULE-6: No accounts or passwords; anyone can pick anyone's name; every change logs the acting person, as evidence for SM-5.
- Parent RULE-7: Python, FastAPI and SQLite; built and tested on the user's computer; hosted per architecture AD-11.
- Parent RULE-9: Every feature works in a browser on laptop and phone; Manage rooms is laptop-first and a simple list on phone.
- Parent Constraints, Rollout: Office managers check their office's rooms on the live app before go-live, so this epic reaches production before epic-find-and-book.
- User, 2026-11-12: Integrated verification runs with Playwright for Python at laptop and phone widths.

## Done when

- On the deployed app, a person picks their name from the seeded people, the app shows it throughout, and the device remembers it until they switch.
- An office manager adds, edits, closes and reopens rooms in their own office only; anyone else is refused, including by a direct request.
- A closed room shows as Closed; invalid or duplicate rooms are refused with the reason.
- Offices, people, home offices and office-manager marks load from the seed file with one command, and reloading with HR's list keeps everyone's id.
- Integrated verification on the deployed app passes, on laptop and phone.

## Boundaries

- Not here: finding free rooms, bookings, refusing bookings of a closed room, the future-booking count when closing, or what happens to those bookings; all epic-find-and-book.
- Not here: the calendar; epic-my-calendar.
- Not here: editing people or offices inside the app (initiative Boundaries).
- Owns for later epics: the shell (top bar with the current name, tabs, DESIGN.md tokens), the people picker, the current person and the office-manager check.

- parent — _bmad-output/initiative-company-room-booking/initiative-company-room-booking.md, section Requirements (R1 to R5) and Constraints
- architecture — _bmad-output/initiative-company-room-booking/architecture-company-room-booking/architecture-company-room-booking.md, AD-1, AD-2, AD-3, AD-6, AD-7, AD-9, AD-10, AD-11, AD-12, Consistency Conventions, Stack, Structural Seed
- experience — _bmad-output/initiative-company-room-booking/ux-company-room-booking/EXPERIENCE.md, Name picker, Rooms table, State Patterns, Responsive & Platform, UJ-4
- design — _bmad-output/initiative-company-room-booking/ux-company-room-booking/DESIGN.md

- Open question: Where the code is hosted, which decides CI. Owner: user. Blocks CI only; `uv run pytest` is the check until then.

Office managers can enter and check their rooms on the live app before go-live, as the initiative's rollout asks.

## Outcome

Office managers in London, Manchester and Leeds keep an accurate room list on the deployed app, so the rooms exist before anyone books (initiative R1 to R5).

## Requirements

- R1 (parent R1): A person picks their name from the seeded active people by typing part of it, then uses the app as that person; their name shows in the top bar on every page.
- R2 (parent R2): A person switches name from the top bar at any time; the device remembers the picked name until they switch; a missing, unknown or inactive name opens Pick your name and then returns to the page asked for.
- R3 (parent R3; user 2026-11-12): An office manager adds a room to their office with a name and a capacity; it appears in their rooms table as Open.
- R4 (parent R4; user 2026-11-12): An office manager edits the name and capacity of a room in their office.
- R5 (parent R5): An office manager closes and reopens a room in their office; a closed room shows as Closed and a reopened one as Open.
- R6 (parent RULE-4; experience State Patterns): Anyone who is not an office manager of a room's office is refused adding, editing, closing or reopening its rooms, even by a direct request; the Manage rooms tab shows only to office managers, and a direct link shows "Only office managers can manage rooms."
- R7 (user 2026-11-12): A room with an empty name, a capacity that is not a whole number of 1 or more, or a name already used in its office is refused with the reason, and the form keeps its values.
- R8 (parent Constraints, seed file; user 2026-11-12): One command loads offices, people, home offices and office-manager marks from a CSV with columns `email, name, office, office_manager`; a reload updates people matched on email and marks anyone missing from it inactive, keeping their id; the same command loads the build seed and HR's list.
- R9 (user 2026-11-12): Tabs show only for screens that exist; until epic-find-and-book ships Rooms, after picking a name an office manager lands on Manage rooms and anyone else on a page with their name and "Booking opens soon."

## Constraints

- Parent RULE-4: Only office managers add, edit, close or reopen rooms, and only in their home office.
- Parent RULE-6: No accounts or passwords; anyone can pick anyone's name; every change logs the acting person, as evidence for SM-5.
- Parent RULE-7: Python, FastAPI and SQLite; built and tested on the user's computer; hosted per architecture AD-11.
- Parent RULE-9: Every feature works in a browser on laptop and phone; Manage rooms is laptop-first and a simple list on phone.
- Parent Constraints, Rollout: Office managers check their office's rooms on the live app before go-live, so this epic reaches production before epic-find-and-book.
- User, 2026-11-12: Integrated verification runs with Playwright for Python at laptop and phone widths.

## Done when

- On the deployed app, a person picks their name from the seeded people, the app shows it throughout, and the device remembers it until they switch.
- An office manager adds, edits, closes and reopens rooms in their own office only; anyone else is refused, including by a direct request.
- A closed room shows as Closed; invalid or duplicate rooms are refused with the reason.
- Offices, people, home offices and office-manager marks load from the seed file with one command, and reloading with HR's list keeps everyone's id.
- Integrated verification on the deployed app passes, on laptop and phone.

## Boundaries

- Not here: finding free rooms, bookings, refusing bookings of a closed room, the future-booking count when closing, or what happens to those bookings; all epic-find-and-book.
- Not here: the calendar; epic-my-calendar.
- Not here: editing people or offices inside the app (initiative Boundaries).
- Owns for later epics: the shell (top bar with the current name, tabs, DESIGN.md tokens), the people picker, the current person and the office-manager check.

**What it holds now:**

  - room validation;

- **6 constraints** from the initiative and your Playwright choice.

Two checks ran before the commit. The first found that R4 (editing a room) didn't say what shows it worked, so it now says the rooms table shows the new values. The second confirmed every line the epic takes from the initiative is in it.

I wrote two files, both in `_bmad-output/initiative-company-room-booking/tickets/epic-offices-and-rooms/`:
- `epic-offices-and-rooms.md`, the epic itself;
- `.memlog.md`, its decision log.

**Still open:**
- **Open question: hosting provider and company-network-only access (OQ-4).** This is for you and IT. It blocks the "stand up on the company host" story, and so the epic can't close, but nothing else waits on it.
- **Open question: where the code will be hosted.** This decides CI. Until then, `uv run pytest` is the check.

- **Assumption:** only company networks can reach the app.

I can go through any of these with you. Otherwise, the next step is to **plan epic 1's stories**: the first is the thinnest path through every layer, and a "Refactor sweep" story closes the epic. Shall I draft them?

# A container's agreed children, in its tickets/ folder; tickets.py ignores unknown keys.
# Table order is build order. `id` is permanent, never reused.
# One kind of table per file: an initiative with no epics uses [[entry]] tables, a parent initiative [[initiative]] tables.
# No status here: the plan carries `status`; `tickets.py mirror` writes `tracker_status` to the leaf.
# next_id = 7 # written by `tickets.py move`; the folder's counter never goes below it

# ---- In an epic's tickets/ folder: one table per planned story, spike, or bug ----

[[entry]]
id = 1 # leaf file's `id:`
type = "story" # story | spike | bug
title = "Cart service scaffold"
description = "Stands up the cart service with one add-item path through UI, API, and store."
verify = "A shopper adds one item on the deployed site and sees it in the cart."
covers = ["R1"] # epic Requirements ids
after = [] # prerequisites only, not sequence
hitl = true # a person runs the starter
risk = "low" # low | medium | high
# estimate = 2 # only if the user gives one
# unknown = "..." # one-sentence user question; `tickets.py next` blocks the entry until removed
# references = ["architecture-checkout/architecture-checkout.md#ad-8"] # beyond the epic's References; pull copies to the ticket
# notes = ["..."] # user's words only; pull copies to Notes
# refine = true # refine to full acceptance criteria first
# plan_checkpoint = true # a person reviews the ticket or plan first
# done_checkpoint = true # pause after it until a person says continue

[[entry]]
id = 2
type = "story"
title = "Apply and refuse discount codes"
description = "Adds code validation to the pricing call and shows the refusal reason."
verify = "A valid code lowers the total; an expired one is refused with its reason."
covers = ["R2", "R3"]
after = [1, "1.3"] # sibling id; "<epic id>.<entry id>"; "epic-<slug>"
hitl = false
risk = "medium"

# ---- In an initiative's tickets/ folder: one table per epic ----

[[epic]]
id = 1
slug = "epic-pricing-rules" # the epic's folder, inside this tickets/ folder
title = "Pricing rules"
description = "Every price a shopper sees comes from one pricing function, deployed." # what is true when it is done; seeds the envelope's Outcome
covers = ["R1", "R2"]

[[epic]]
id = 2
slug = "epic-cart-rules"
title = "Shoppers manage their cart"
description = "A shopper adds, changes and removes items on the deployed site and the total follows."
covers = ["R3", "R4", "R5"]
after = [{ epic = 1, needs = "the one-function pricing contract" }] # entries carry their own `after`

# ---- In a parent initiative's tickets/ folder: one table per child initiative ----

[[initiative]]
id = 1
slug = "initiative-storefront" # the child's folder, beside the parent's
title = "Shoppers buy online"
description = "A shopper finds, prices and pays for an order on the live site."
covers = ["R1", "R2"]

[[initiative]]
id = 2
slug = "initiative-fulfillment"
title = "Orders ship themselves"
description = "A paid order is picked, packed and tracked without manual steps."
covers = ["R3"]
after = [{ initiative = 1, needs = "the order-paid event" }]

- **Proposed child initiatives or epics, an epic breakdown, or a re-slice:** always, on the draft `tickets.toml` before approval. First run the Dependencies section yourself and fix the draft; give the agent its path. Show what the check changed and confirmed. Rerun when the user adds, removes, merges, or reorders items. At initiative slicing, check scope ownership; future epics need no stories or full detail.
- **A refined ticket:** before execution.
- **A container:** before closure, its implemented coverage and Done when.

How:

- Per epic: its container, its `tickets.toml`, every child ticket, done ones too, its Requirements, its `sources:` files, companions; sections Ticket, Set, Dependencies. The tree: the initiative, its `tickets.toml`, the epic files once written (on a parent, each child initiative's file), its `sources:` files; sections Tree, Dependencies. A single ticket: its epic file; section Ticket. Closure: section Closure.
- Name the `refined: true` tickets; point the agent at "Rules the template cannot carry" in `/home/claude/runs/room-booker/_bmad/render/bmad-agent-po/room-booker-72ea137e33d5/29ecc89ff22a7f491c6e/references/ticket.md`. Once `tickets.toml` exists, give the full `tickets.py status` command for the folder.
- Sort findings into fix (mechanical), suggest (with reason), or ask the user. Resolve gaps, missing prerequisites, and contradictions before proceeding; the user decides suggestions and scope changes.
- Do not re-raise suggestions declined in a `Decision:` line unless new evidence changes their basis.

# Validation checks

`validate.md` assigns sections to agents.

## Ticket

- References open; no unfilled placeholders; assumptions marked.
- Nothing contradicts its epic file, its companions, the architecture, or a recorded decision.
- Each entry has a description, `unknown` when one is known, and a `verify` a non-builder can run; only bugs, `refine = true` entries, and leaves with no entry need full criteria before execution.
- A ticket needing full criteria and covering an id in a `Source conflict:` line with no later `Decision:` has `refined: false`.


## Set

Every entry in the epic's `tickets.toml`, draft or committed, pulled or not.

- Tickets cover every Requirements line not deferred with the user; each `covers` id exists there; tickets sharing an id say which part each delivers.
- UX, architecture, constraint and integration work is covered without ids; results satisfy Done when; citing an id alone is not coverage.
- Every `after`, cross-epic too, is a real prerequisite, not restated order; once `tickets.toml` exists, `tickets.py status` on the epic shows no cycle, `drift`, `unpinned_after`, `undeclared_after`, or `order_conflict`; the epic's Notes hold a dated `Decision:` line naming the tracer bullet, and the sequencing decisions.
- A builder could write each story's acceptance criteria from the epic, entry, and references; if not, fix the epic, not the one-sentence `description` and `verify`.
- Tracer bullet, as rendered in `slice.md`: The first entry is the tracer bullet: the thinnest path through every layer the epic touches. Its setup, including any starter the user runs, is a hitl step. It and any demoable entry say what someone sees running when done. Next is the story the user is least sure of.
- Refactor sweep, as rendered in `slice.md`: An epic of more than three entries closes with a story "Refactor sweep" that waits on every other entry except a closing end-to-end suite. Its scope, set at its start from plans and review findings the epic deferred, is cleanup only; scope pushed out of another story is a new story. Propose it by default; if declined, record a `Decision:` line in the epic's Notes.


## Tree

The initiative, its `tickets.toml`, draft or committed, and the epic files once written; for a parent initiative, the child initiatives in place of epics.

- Every initiative requirement has an accountable epic or agreed deferral; shared ones say which part each epic delivers; no unexplained overlap.
- Each epic's `covers` cites parent ids; each Requirements line names in parentheses its parent id, or its source section if the parent lacks it; a child's `covers` resolves through the Requirements line to a parent id.
- Every source id on a Requirements line exists in a `sources:` file, every parent id in the parent's Requirements; every adopted design or architecture document is in `companions:`.
- Every unit the source touches is an epic, out of scope, or a touch point (consumed or configured only, named in the initiative's Boundaries with its owner).
- Each decision several epics adopt has one home: an architecture spine section, or an opening-epic entry (first `[[epic]]`) the others wait on.
- Every written epic file has Outcome, Done when (including production delivery), Boundaries, its `covers`, and references; one with `refined: false` needs no Requirements or breakdown yet; the initiative's `tickets.toml` lists every epic in build order, each `after` naming what it needs, and `tickets.py status` on the initiative shows no cycle or `order_conflict`; it opens with a platform-baseline epic, or its first epic's first stories, or a `Decision:` line saying why not.
- A parent initiative's `tickets.toml` lists every child in build order, each `after` naming what it needs; every child's `sources:` lists the parent's file; `tickets.py status` on the parent shows no `order_conflict`.
- The initiative's `tickets.toml` lists child initiatives, epics, or entries, one kind only; with epics, no leaf sits in the initiative's `tickets/` folder.


## Dependencies

An item is a set entry, a tree epic, or a parent's child initiative.

- Needs: what each item needs to start and to run its check is built by it or its `after`.
- Collisions: items with no dependency path share no code, config, schema, or setup; else add an `after` or merge them.
- Shared setup: the earliest item needing it owns it; others list it in `after`.
- Handoffs: when one item relies on another's output, both descriptions say so.


## Closure

- Verify the container's Done when, requirements, constraints and companions against implementation evidence, not child status; explain dropped work and confirm remaining scope with the user.

🎯 Here's the draft for epic 1: nine stories, in build order. The ticket tool reports no problems. I ran the coverage, ticket and dependency checks myself rather than in a fresh session, and fixed what they found.

| # | Story | Covers | Waits on | Needs a person |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Pick your name, end to end:** first, thinnest version through every layer | R1, R8 (first load) | — | yes: you install Python 3.14 and uv, then run it locally |
| 2 | **Deploy bundle runs locally:** Docker, Caddy, Litestream; restore from backup checked | — | 1 | |
| 3 | **App stands up on the company host** | — | 2 | yes, with IT · ⛔ **blocked by OQ-4** |
| 4 | **CI runs the tests on every push** | — | 1 | yes · ⛔ **blocked by where the code is hosted** |
| 5 | **Switch name and reload people safely:** remembered cookie, return to the page asked for, HR reload keeps ids | R2, R8 (reload) | 1 | |
| 6 | **Office managers add rooms:** Manage rooms tab, the check, validation, landing pages | R3, R6, R7, R9 | 5 | |
| 7 | **Office managers edit, close and reopen rooms** | R4, R5, R6, R7 | 6 | |
| 8 | **Refactor sweep:** cleanup only, from what 1–7 deferred | — | 1–7 | |
| 9 | **Integrated verification on the deployed app:** Playwright at laptop and phone widths, plus a real phone | R1–R7, R9 | 8 | yes: run from the company network |

**Why it's cut this way**
- **Story 1 goes first.** It's the thinnest path through scaffold, migration, seed, service, page, shell and tests. When it's done you see the app running locally: you pick your name and it shows in the top bar. It also builds the Playwright harness and the people table with every column the later stories need.
- **Story 2 comes next because it's the least certain part.** Hosting is the open question, so the packaging is proven early, locally, where nothing blocks it.
- **Work that can run in parallel after story 1:**
  - the deploy lane (2 → 3);
  - CI (4);
  - people and rooms (5 → 6 → 7).

  Story 6 waits on 5 because both change the people service and the shell.
- **Merges.** I folded "switch name" into the seed reload because both are about the current person. I folded edit and close/reopen into one story because they're row actions on the same table. Each alone would have had more setup than work.
- **Story 9** wasn't required by default. I added it because the Done when asks for integrated verification on the deployed app.

**What this means for closing the epic.** Stories 3 and 4 are blocked until you answer the hosting and code-host questions. The sweep waits on them, and so does verification, so the epic can't close until both are answered. Stories 1, 2, 5, 6 and 7 can all be built now.

**Left to epic 2 (`epic-find-and-book`):** the future-booking count on the close confirmation, and what happens to those bookings.

Say yes to commit this as it stands, or tell me what to change: merge, split, reorder or drop.

content.text:
🎯 I've cut the draft down to two stories that both run on your computer. The ticket tool reports no problems.

| # | Story | Covers | Waits on | Needs a person |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Pick and switch your name, end to end.** This is the first, thinnest version through every layer. It sets up the project, the people table, seed load and reload, Pick your name with type-ahead, and the top-bar shell. It also adds the remembered name with return to the page you asked for, switching name, and the Playwright harness. | R1, R2, R8 | — | yes: you install Python 3.14 and uv, then run it locally |
| 2 | **Office managers manage their office's rooms.** It covers add, edit, close and reopen, the office-manager check, validation, the refusal message, logging who made each change, and landing office managers on Manage rooms. | R3–R7, R9 | 1 | |

Between them the two stories cover all nine requirements. With only two stories, the epic doesn't need a refactor sweep or a closing end-to-end story.

**Before you approve, the trade-off:**
- **The epic still won't be finished after these two stories.** Its Done when requires the app on the company host, and the initiative's rollout needs office managers to check their rooms on the live app. Deployment, CI and verification on the deployed app are deferred, not dropped. I'll record that as a dated decision and keep the Done when unchanged. So epic 1 stays open until you ask me to plan those stories, probably once OQ-4 is answered. Epic 2 waits on "the deployed app", so that gate stays too.
- **Both stories are large for a single build session**, story 2 especially. If a build struggles, the natural split is "add rooms" and "edit, close, reopen".
- **Nothing is blocked now.** The hosting and code-host questions moved off the stories and back to the epic's Open questions.

On a yes I'll commit the breakdown. With it I'll update the epic's notes: the first story, the deferral, the two merges, and the epic's risk unchanged at medium. Then story 1 is ready for `bmad-build`.
